prompt: Explain how to check disk usage on Windows in a practical way.

newMessages.text: Explain how to check disk usage on Windows in a practical way.

Use this 3-step workflow on Windows:

1. Check how full each drive is  
`File Explorer` -> `This PC`  
You’ll see each drive’s used/free bar immediately.

2. See what is taking space  
`Settings` -> `System` -> `Storage` -> click your drive (usually `C:`)  
This gives a category breakdown (`Apps`, `Temporary files`, `Documents`, etc.) and is the most practical built-in view.

3. Get exact numbers in PowerShell  
```powershell
Get-PSDrive -PSProvider FileSystem |
Select-Object Name,
@{N='Used(GB)';E={[math]::Round($_.Used/1GB,2)}},
@{N='Free(GB)';E={[math]::Round($_.Free/1GB,2)}}
```

If you want, I can also give you a safe command to list the top 20 largest files on `C:`.
